stories.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions until 2051
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a Constitutional Amendment Bill to freeze the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats until 2051. The move aims to address concerns regarding proportionate strength, marking a shift from an earlier proposal that sought to redistribute seats based on the 2011 Census population.

stories.title: Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation
stories.summary: The amendments in the Constitution being proposed in a Bill approved by the Union Cabinet propose to continue the existing proportion of strength in the Lok Sabha of individual States for another 25 years, until 2051. stories.title: Cabinet approves 50 percent increase in Lok Sabha seats
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a Constitution amendment bill to increase Lok Sabha seats by 50 percent for all states while freezing current seat shares until 2051. The proposal aims to implement women's reservation through delimitation, following the rejection of a previous attempt by the Opposition in April.

stories.title: Accused shot during exchange of fire with police in Asansol
stories.summary: Pratap Das, an accused wanted for robbery, theft, and cyber fraud, was shot in the leg during an exchange of fire with police in Asansol on Friday. Officers were attempting to arrest him at a hideout in the Ismail area when the incident occurred.

stories.title: Omar Abdullah denies blacktopping on Amarnath route
stories.summary: Chief Minister Omar Abdullah denied that any blacktopping had been performed on the Amarnath route. He accused the BJP and PDP of attempting to foment discord between Hindus and Muslims by alleging that such work had taken place. He challenged his opponents to provide proof.

stories.title: TVK MLA arrested for harassing IAS officer
stories.summary: Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh was arrested on Friday for allegedly harassing a woman IAS officer. The arrest followed a directive from the Madras High Court, which ordered the State Public Prosecutor to engage with the officer after she filed a formal complaint regarding inappropriate advances.

stories.title: Syed Faisal Qadri appointed Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir
stories.summary: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir on Friday. The position had remained vacant for more than two years. The appointment follows a proposal forwarded to the Lieutenant Governor eight months ago.

stories.title: Modi invokes Lord Murugan following Supreme Court directive
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi invoked Lord Murugan on social media after the Supreme Court ordered the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at Thirupparankundram. The BJP welcomed the ruling as a victory for devotees, accusing the Tamil Nadu government of acting against the Hindu community.

stories.title: Yogi Adityanath questions Samajwadi Party employment record
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath challenged the Samajwadi Party to account for its past governance record. He claimed the current BJP administration has made twice as many government appointments as the SP and BSP combined, following the SP's promise of 25 lakh jobs in its manifesto.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu sanctions funds for road upgrades
stories.summary: The government has allocated ₹1,037.7 crore to upgrade 340 village and panchayat union roads to Other District Road standards. The project covers 797.13 km across four regions, with the Coimbatore region receiving the largest share of the funding at ₹410.77 crore.

stories.title: Family dies by suicide in Vizianagaram
stories.summary: Three members of a family died after jumping in front of a goods train on Friday. Police stated the family faced financial difficulties. The victims included a 53-year-old man, his 50-year-old wife, and their 25-year-old son, who worked at a local Village Secretariat.

stories.title: Mother protests for CBI probe into son's death
stories.summary: Asha Devi has begun a fast-unto-death protest, claiming the Bihar government failed to fulfill assurances regarding her son's death. Bharat Bhushan Tiwari was allegedly killed in a police encounter in June. Independent MP Pappu Yadav has joined the protest to demand a CBI inquiry.

stories.title: Bus conductor killed in collision with parked lorry
stories.summary: A 57-year-old transport corporation conductor died after his bus struck a lorry parked on the carriageway near Chengam. Ten passengers were injured in the incident. The lorry driver had reportedly left the vehicle on the road to search for a mechanic after a flat tyre.

stories.title: Farmer arrested for homemade gun possession
stories.summary: Police arrested a 25-year-old farmer in Vellore after discovering a homemade gun, explosives, and hunting equipment on his property. The man told authorities he learned to build the weapons via online videos to hunt animals and protect crops from wild boars.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders temple ritual and suspends trustees
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ordered the Karthigai Deepam to be lit on the stone pillar at the Thirupparankundram temple, citing wilful disobedience by state authorities and trustees. The court suspended the Board of Trustees and appointed two former High Court judges to oversee the management.

stories.title: Global fashion brands move orders from Bangladesh to India
stories.summary: Retailers including Zara and H&M diverted $254 million in orders from Bangladesh to India during early November. Factory owners cited labour unrest, energy shortages, and rising costs as reasons for the shift. The move marks a significant disruption to a key pillar of the Bangladeshi economy.

stories.title: GITAM University opens admissions for 2027-28
stories.summary: GITAM Deemed to be University has opened applications for 111 undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. Admissions will be determined by the GITAM Admission Test, scheduled for March 27, 2027. The deadline for prospective students to submit their applications is March 24.

stories.title: Telangana grievance platform wins national award
stories.summary: The Telangana government's Prajavani platform received the Digital Transformation Excellence award at the Parivartan Awards 2026. The platform was recognized for its role in making grievance redressal more transparent and accountable. It was developed by the state government with technical support from the Centre for Good Governance.

stories.title: SpiceJet experiences technical disruption
stories.summary: SpiceJet reported a website glitch that affected passenger check-in and payment processing. The airline has advised travellers to arrive at airports early to account for the service interruption. The company did not specify when full functionality would be restored.

stories.title: Stars vs. warning labels: Inside packaged food dispute and what the SC ruling means
stories.summary: Chetan Chauhan is the National Affairs Editor looking into all aspects of news and features from across India. A Chevening scholar with over three decades of experience in reporting and news management, Chetan has extensively covered all important aspects of the social sector, political economy, environment and climate change nationally

stories.title: Assam police bust fake certificate scheme
stories.summary: Authorities have arrested three individuals suspected of selling forged Class 10 pass certificates. The operation reportedly involved 4,900 students who allegedly purchased the fraudulent documents. Police are continuing their investigation into the scale of the operation.

stories.title: FSSAI initiates prosecution against Bisleri
stories.summary: The food regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International after water samples from its West Bengal plant tested positive for coliform bacteria. This follows a similar action taken earlier this week regarding a sample collected from the company's facility in Goa.

stories.title: Bisleri faces second prosecution for bacterial contamination
stories.summary: The FSSAI has initiated legal action against Bisleri International after a sample from its West Bengal plant tested positive for coliform bacteria. This is the second prosecution this week, following a similar finding at the company's Goa facility. The regulator previously prohibited a specific batch in August.

stories.title: Semiconductor research centre opens in Chennai
stories.summary: Rajalakshmi Engineering College has inaugurated a Centre of Excellence on Semiconductor Prototype, Advanced Research, and Commercialisation. The facility is intended to provide students and faculty with a platform for research, hands-on learning, and prototype development in the semiconductor field.

stories.title: IIT-Madras updates B.Tech curriculum
stories.summary: IIT-Madras has introduced a six-month industry placement programme for B.Tech students, starting in January 2027. The initiative replaces the traditional two-month summer model to increase industry engagement. The university expects the change to improve career readiness by allowing students to work on real-world challenges.

stories.title: Chennai Mayor to pursue legal action over AI video
stories.summary: Chennai Mayor R. Priya announced legal action against a group allegedly linked to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam leadership. The move follows the circulation of an AI-generated video portraying her in a vulgar manner. The Mayor stated this is not the first time she has faced such attacks.

stories.title: Entrepreneur donates gold to Tirumala temple
stories.summary: Vardhman Jain, co-founder of Access Healthcare, donated 121 kg of gold ornaments valued at ₹207.6 crore to the Tirumala temple. The offering was presented to authorities in the presence of the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister. It is considered one of the largest recent donations to the deity.

stories.title: Karnataka government issues show-cause notice to IOCL terminal
stories.summary: The Karnataka government has directed Indian Oil Corporation Limited to explain discrepancies in ethanol and motor gasoline measurements at its Bengaluru terminal. State inspections previously identified ethanol blending levels as high as 32 percent in some local petrol samples. The company has seven days to respond.

stories.title: Bengaluru washermen restrict operations as water sources dry up
stories.summary: Facing a severe drought, Bengaluru dhobi ghats have transitioned to water tankers and alternate-day washing schedules. The city's 31 historic facilities require up to 100,000 litres of water daily, but local borewells have largely failed. The city's century-old washing infrastructure is currently struggling to find water.

stories.title: Former ISRO chief calls for environmental safety in tech
stories.summary: Former ISRO Chairman A.S. Kiran Kumar stated that scientific innovations must prioritise environmental safety and sustainability. Speaking at an international toxicology convention, he noted that space technology should serve as an instrument for societal welfare. Technology is now being asked to consider its own consequences.

stories.summary: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said Telangana had sufficient food stocks to meet its requirements for the next two years, the availability of water remained a major concern due to El Nino-induced drought, and urged people to rise above political considerations to address the looming water crisis. stories.title: 25 workers, including nine children, rescued from bonded labour in Hanumakonda
stories.summary: Twenty-five workers, including nine children, who had been held in bonded labour for periods extending up to 14 years at two cement ring and brick manufacturing units in Kamalapur village of Hanumakonda district, were rescued by district authorities on Thursday following a complaint from social workers. stories.title: Dehradun seals six restaurants for environmental violations
stories.summary: Authorities in Dehradun have sealed six restaurants on Rajpur Road, including a KFC outlet, for failing to comply with environmental norms. The Uttarakhand Pollution Control Board issued show-cause notices to the establishments one month ago. The administration took action after receiving no satisfactory response from the operators.

stories.title: Maharashtra mandates check dams for all new bridge projects
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government has made it mandatory to construct a one-metre-high check dam alongside every new bridge project. The policy aims to increase water storage capacity across the state. The decision follows a cabinet sub-committee meeting focused on drought mitigation strategies for the region.

stories.title: India sugar stocks may drop as production falls
stories.summary: India's sugar closing stock is projected to shrink to 2 million tonnes due to declining production. The industry is concerned that El Nino may further impact the outlook for the next season, complicating efforts to maintain high domestic supply levels.

stories.title: Guindy Children’s Park closes following bird deaths
stories.summary: Chennai's Guindy Children’s Park will remain closed until November 30 after several birds died at the facility. Officials have sent samples to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases for testing. The closure is described as a precautionary measure while the cause remains unknown.

stories.title: Wayanad declared India’s first e-waste-free district
stories.summary: Wayanad has been named India’s first e-waste-free model district following a two-month collection drive. Local volunteers and government institutions gathered 102.8 tonnes of discarded electronics, including mobile phones and household appliances. The district now claims to have cleared its inventory of old electronic items.

stories.title: US Air Force pauses Cloud One migration after breach
stories.summary: The US Air Force has reportedly paused efforts to migrate back-office applications to its Cloud One platform following a security breach. Updates to existing applications on the system have also been blocked, preventing personnel from applying fixes. The Air Force declined to comment on the system status.

stories.title: US goods trade deficit expands to $149.5 billion
stories.summary: The US goods trade deficit widened by 10.7 percent in October to $149.5 billion, exceeding economist forecasts of $133 billion. While imports rose significantly, the government noted that trade previously subtracted 3.21 percentage points from third-quarter GDP growth, which was offset by AI-related business investment.

stories.title: Zelenskyy warns of global food supply risks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia's war has significantly disrupted agricultural exports from the Black Sea region. He warned that the resulting difficulties in shipping grain, flour, and sunflower oil threaten food supplies for hundreds of millions of people worldwide.

stories.title: SAP weighs cutting 10,000 jobs in AI restructuring
stories.summary: SAP is considering a restructuring plan that could affect at least 9% of its 110,000 employees. CEO Christian Klein aims to transform the company into an AI-first organization, with product, engineering, and sales teams under review. The final headcount reduction remains subject to ongoing labor negotiations.

stories.title: Government plans marketing campaign for Indian tea
stories.summary: The government is launching an international marketing campaign and providing freight support to help Indian tea exporters. The initiative aims to improve the competitiveness of domestic tea in global markets by easing transportation costs and securing better prices for the industry.

stories.title: Arabic language conference discusses AI
stories.summary: An international conference at Anvarul Islam Arabic College recently explored the intersection of digital humanities and the Arabic language. Attendees observed that while AI may alter how the language is used, human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of current technology.

stories.title: Security, Religion, Kashmir: Pak-Linked Deepfake Campaign Targets India
stories.summary: Social media accounts often styled themselves as Indian.

stories.title: Security tips for wedding invitation QR codes
stories.summary: Wedding guests are being advised to verify the source of digital invitations before scanning QR codes. Experts warn that scanning unfamiliar links can lead to online scams or banking fraud. Users are cautioned never to share sensitive financial information or one-time passwords through these platforms.

stories.title: Nagaland repatriates ancestral remains from UK museum
stories.summary: Thirty-nine Naga ancestral remains have returned to Nagaland after a six-year repatriation process from the Pitt Rivers Museum in the UK. The remains were flown to Dimapur and escorted to Kohima for a formal homecoming program and dignified burial by members of various Naga tribes.

stories.summary: Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on

stories.title: Gandhi Hospital performs free cochlear implant
stories.summary: Doctors at Gandhi Hospital in Hyderabad performed a cochlear implant surgery on an eight-year-old boy with congenital hearing loss. The procedure and subsequent year of auditory verbal therapy were sponsored by the Chief Minister’s Relief Fund, providing a service that costs over 10 lakh at private hospitals.

stories.title: Restaurant licence suspended for hygiene violations
stories.summary: The Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs suspended the licence of a restaurant in Karimnagar following an inspection. Officials reported finding raw eggs in mayonnaise, unhygienic meat storage, and improper refrigerator maintenance. The restaurant has been cited for multiple food safety violations.

stories.title: Chinese medical delegation visits Bengaluru hospitals
stories.summary: A 15-member delegation from Guizhou Medical University visited two Bengaluru hospitals this week. The visit, part of a medical mission, focused on exploring healthcare cooperation and knowledge exchange. The team toured various departments and interacted with patients recovering from surgeries.

stories.title: Directors of fertility centre detained in trafficking case
stories.summary: Police detained four directors of the company operating Oasis Fertility and Sadguru ART clinics following raids in Hyderabad. The detentions are connected to an alleged illegal human egg harvesting and trafficking racket. Investigations into the company's corporate offices are ongoing.

stories.title: Health risks of skin-lightening creams highlighted
stories.summary: A 17-year-old in Kerala was hospitalized after using a skin-lightening cream that reportedly contained mercury. The product, marketed as natural, caused severe health symptoms. The case has prompted warnings regarding the safety of unregulated cosmetic products sold through social media influencers.

stories.title: Kochi survey reveals sewage treatment gaps
stories.summary: A survey by the Kerala Water Authority found that many households in central Kochi discharge sewage into waterbodies. While most establishments use septic tanks, the agency noted they are scientifically inadequate, leading to groundwater pollution. High population density and space constraints have hindered effective waste management.

stories.title: CDS General Subramani discusses regional space developments
stories.summary: Defence Editor Rahul Singh reported that CDS General Subramani has flagged Pakistan's space growth, which is allegedly aided by China and Turkey. The General suggested that these developments must be factored into India's national security calculus. Space is becoming increasingly crowded with strategic interests.

stories.title: Experts discuss the complexities of conducting the Census
stories.summary: Retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and professor Vinay Sitapati discussed the challenges of the Indian Census, including the need for governing laws and the training of enumerators. The conversation covered the evolution of census motives since independence and its implications for delimitation. Counting remains a complicated task.

stories.title: Ramdev shifts focus from BJP support to government criticism
stories.summary: Yoga guru Ramdev, who rose to prominence supporting the BJP's 2014 campaign, has begun criticising the government over recruitment corruption and school facilities. He has also targeted Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, a figure with close ties to the BJP leadership. The former ally is now a critic.

stories.title: Saurav Das addresses citizenship claims on television
stories.summary: Saurav Das appeared on Piers Morgan Uncensored to state he was born in Delhi and is Indian. He addressed allegations regarding his birth certificate and family lineage, noting that many people of his generation lack formal documentation. Citizenship remains a topic of public debate.
